title: Anonymous usage analytics on Cloudflare
summary: The game now records anonymous, cookie-free usage events to a Cloudflare Workers Analytics Engine dataset so we can see how people play: sessions, Single Player vs Multiplayer, Freeride vs Race, venues, vehicles, riding time, race results, load times and load failures.
details: New POST /api/events Worker endpoint validates every event against a fixed schema (shared web/analytics.js) and writes it to the fury_usage dataset with only a two-letter country and the release commit added.
No cookies, identifiers, player names, room codes, URLs or free text are sent; IPs only key a 60-events-per-minute rate limiter and are never stored.
Automated browsers, local hosts, Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control send nothing; analytics failures never affect play.
Cloudflare Web Analytics (page views, referrers, Core Web Vitals) is ready behind an optional public site token; the CSP admits its beacon only when configured.
tools/analytics_report.py summarizes the dataset; research/ANALYTICS.md documents the schema and setup.

Verification: 192 Node tests (191 pass, 1 pre-existing private-content skip) including new client and Worker analytics tests, repository/secret scans, release packaging tests, a Wrangler dry-run showing the USAGE and EVENT_LIMIT bindings, and the content-free browser smoke group (4/4).
limitation: Host verification only at the time of writing. Production event delivery has not yet been checked on the public app. Cloudflare Web Analytics stays off until a site token is created in the dashboard, and reading the dataset needs an Account Analytics Read API token.
